segments.heading: The one line: a tag, then the arguments of bwx12
segments.text:
One line for the runner script `rx.sh`: a tag, the character `|`, and the argument list of one bwx12 process. `rx.sh` passes the argument list without quotes. So the shell splits it at the spaces into 21 arguments [Ref2]. Each bullet below is one field or option, as the function `main` of `bwx12.c` reads it [Ref1].
- `a6456`: the tag. `rx.sh` writes the standard output of the process to the file `a6456.csv`, and it writes the tag into `launches.txt`. bwx12 does not receive the tag.
- `--threads 120`: start 120 worker threads.
- `--cpus 0-63,64-119`: the CPU list 0 to 119. Thread number i is pinned to entry i of the list. So 64 threads run on mesh 0 (CPUs 0-63) and 56 threads run on mesh 1 (CPUs 64-119).
- `--bytes 256M`: the buffer size per thread, 256 MiB (268435456 bytes). Each thread allocates its own buffer and writes it once before the first interval. Every kernel of `--seq` works on this whole size.
- `--stop common`: all threads start an interval at one common start time and stop at one common deadline. A thread reads the clock after each chunk of 2 MiB. It stops at the first clock value that is not before the deadline.
- `--start common`: each thread starts every interval at byte 0 of its own buffer. The option sets the start position in the buffer, not the start time. It is also the default.
- `--min-ms 6000`: the length of a timed interval. The deadline is 6000 ms (6 s) after the common start time.
- `--rounds 2`: run the whole kernel sequence 2 times in the same process (round 0 and round 1).
- `--seq oldread,asmread,read_nop96,read_nop256,read_1pl`: the kernels to time, one interval each, in this order (positions 0 to 4). 5 kernels in 2 rounds give 10 timed intervals. `oldread` is the old read kernel. `asmread` is the hand-written load-only loop. The other three are test loops.
- `--count`: each thread also reads hardware counters directly before and directly after every interval. The csv file gets one `C` row per thread and interval.
- `--pmu-type 11`: the type number of the counter unit. bwx12 passes it to Linux in the field `type` of `perf_event_attr`. A listing from CRB of 2026-11-13 shows 11 as the type of `armv8_pmuv3_0`, the counter unit of the CPU cores [Ref6].
- `--events cbusy0=0x198,cbusy1=0x199,cbusy2=0x19a,cbusy3=0x19b,cbusy_mt=0x19c,bus_access=0x19`: six events, each written as NAME=CODE. NAME is the column title in the `C` rows. CODE selects the event. Linux gets it in the field `config`. Codes 0x198 to 0x19b count the responses that the core received with busy level 0, 1, 2 and 3. The busy level is a number from 0 to 3 that the mesh sends to a core with each answer [Ref12]. Code 0x19c counts the responses with the flag "CBusy Multi-threaded" set. Code 0x19 counts bus accesses [Ref5].
